name: Gradient PLA
chemical_makeup: Chemically identical to base PLA — the variation is a manufacturing technique in which pigment streams are blended along the filament length so colour shifts gradually down the spool
summary: Base PLA with a colour-blending manufacturing process and no chemistry change: pigment is graded along the strand so a tall print shifts colour with height. Printing, drying, feeding, mechanical and thermal behaviour are all base-PLA-equivalent; the only real deltas are price (~$25/kg vs ~$18-20/kg) and the design constraint that the part must be tall or long enough for the transition to develop.

printing.notes: No printing delta versus base PLA — Bambu's material table groups plain (non-silk) gradient PLA with PLA Basic at 190-240 °C nozzle and 35-65 °C bed. Unfilled and non-abrasive, so a brass nozzle is fine. Caveat: gradient spools are also sold in silk form; a silk-gradient behaves like pla-silk (hotter nozzle, slower outer walls for gloss, weaker layers), not like this entry.

feeding.notes: Because the chemistry is unmodified base PLA, there is no added brittleness, abrasion or snap risk in the feed path — this and pla-matte are the only two of the six aesthetic variants that earn an unqualified 'yes' for AMS/MMU/CFS use. One practical caution that is scheduling rather than mechanical: swapping a gradient spool mid-print restarts the colour position, so keep one spool per part.

drying.dryness_validation: No popping/crackling or steam at the nozzle; glossy consistent extrudate; minimal stringing on a retraction test — same checks as base PLA
drying.notes: Unchanged from base PLA (Bambu 55 °C/8 h, Prusa-style 45 °C/6 h also fine). The pigment blending adds nothing hygroscopic.

storage.recommendations: Sealed bag or drybox with desiccant; same tolerance for open-air storage as base PLA. Keep the spool wound in order — the colour sequence is positional, so re-spooling scrambles the intended gradient

price.notes: Bambu PLA Basic Gradient around $24.99/kg — roughly a 25-40 % premium over base PLA Basic ($18-20/kg) that buys the colour-blending process, not any material improvement

recommended: showpieces where colour transition across height is the design
single-material prints that need to look multi-colour without an AMS
not_recommended: small prints where the transition has no room to develop
batch prints needing consistent colour part-to-part
sustained-load, hot-environment or outdoor parts (same limits as base PLA)

properties.notes: All figures are inherited from the base PLA entry: no manufacturer publishes a separate mechanical datasheet for gradient PLA, and with no filler or additive present the plain gradient formulation is expected to be mechanically and thermally identical to PLA Basic (density ~1.24 g/cm³, Tg ~58 °C, tensile 45-65 MPa). Unverified in isolation — treat as equivalence by chemistry, not by measurement. This is the only one of the six aesthetic variants whose density is unchanged from base PLA; silk 1.27, matte 1.31, glow 1.26, metal 1.25 and wood 1.21 all shift.

compatibility.notes: Identical to base PLA in every bonding respect — welds to PLA grades, does not weld to PETG/ABS/ASA/PC/PA/PP, and is usable as breakaway support for PETG and TPU. Using gradient filament as support is wasteful of an expensive spool but mechanically fine.

plate_recommendations.notes: No delta from base PLA: textured PEI at 35-60 °C bed with no release agent. Smooth PEI or glass equally fine — plate choice does not interact with the gradient effect.

emissions.notes: Identical to base PLA, the lowest-emission common filament; pigment loading is trivial and adds no measured species.

safety_notes: Pigment package is not food-contact certified, as with most coloured PLA.
additional_notes: Distinguish three marketing categories that are often conflated: gradient (colour blended along the strand length, this entry), 'Quantum'/dual-colour (two colours fused side by side for an angle-dependent shimmer), and silk-gradient (a gradient colour scheme layered on top of the silk gloss additive — score and print that as pla-silk). Design tip: gradient period is fixed by the manufacturer, so a part's height determines how much of the transition it shows; vase mode maximises the effect per gram.

provenance.conflicts: No dedicated mechanical TDS exists for gradient PLA — every property and score in this entry is inferred from base-PLA equivalence rather than measured, which is why confidence is 'low' despite the deltas being small. Secondary risk: some vendors sell silk-gradient under the same 'gradient' label; if the spool is silk, the pla-silk entry applies instead (layer adhesion drops to roughly 4/10 and the nozzle temperature window shifts up).
